articles.title: C. elegans Study Reveals Cellular Defense Against Drug-Induced Lysosomal Damage — Implications Pharma Doesn't Want Discussed
articles.summary: A new study in PLOS Biology identifies a xenobiotic defense system in C. elegans that neutralizes cationic amphiphilic drugs — a class that includes widely-prescribed antidepressants, antihistamines, and antipsychotics — by coupling metabolic breakdown to cellular efflux. The finding implies these drugs cause collateral lysosomal damage in humans that the body must actively fight to survive. This is the kind of mechanistic drug-harm research that should be front-page news but instead sits buried in a nematode biology journal.

articles.title: Ergothioneine Compound Shows Promise Against Preeclampsia — Will OB Guidelines Notice or Ignore It?
articles.summary: A new PLOS ONE study finds that the naturally occurring compound L-(+)-ergothioneine significantly ameliorates preeclampsia-associated vascular dysfunction by modulating the Nrf2-PPARγ-sFlt-1 axis — a pathway central to one of pregnancy's most dangerous complications. Preeclampsia kills tens of thousands of mothers annually and current interventions remain limited. Whether this non-patentable finding makes it into obstetric practice or gets quietly shelved is the real test of whether evidence drives medicine.
